question: Is the directional Protected-to-Rice switching probability greater on the source-recorded day-to-night boundary than the night-to-day boundary, after subtracting current seven-category availability weighted by fixed per-birdyear categorical preference? Is reverse Rice-to-Protected switching oppositely organized?

hypotheses.primary: For all four source species, Protected→Rice destination enrichment at day→night exceeds its enrichment at night→day among switches leaving Protected. Report both signs regardless of support; no species rescued by changing thresholds.
hypotheses.reciprocal: Rice→Protected destination enrichment may be higher at night→day than day→night. Report both, including species with insufficient information.

cohort: Same 380578 source rows, 189851 qualified event keys, 329 source birdyears, 56591 original exact-hour pairs, 58 between seasons and 9586 day/night edge pairs. Exactly the 7 original exclusive categories with source Category 'Protected' treated as a management category not a directly observed daytime roost.

effect.y: For each boundary step from the named prior category, 1 if the next destination is the named opposite category (not conditional on whether it switched); expected probability is fitted whole-birdyear static seven-class choice p_t of the named destination under current source time-matched q_t, as in the original California V2 static preference null.
effect.residual: r=y-p_t(destination), examined as mean(r at day→night) minus mean(r at night→day), within each source birdyear × source season for prior category only.
effect.unit: For each distinct source tagged bird candidate ID, average equal-weight qualified birdyear×season contrasts over its tracking years, then equal-weight candidate IDs by species. Require >=2 prior-category observations in both boundary directions per birdyear×season stratum, >=1 such stratum per source individual and >=8 independent candidates per species for inferential interval.
effect.boot: 10,000 seeded source candidate-tag bootstrap replicates, 95% percentile CI and count positive tags; no pooled across-species effect, no multiplicity-adjusted experiment claim.
effect.descriptive: Report real observed destination counts, source available-choice expected counts, eligible stratum counts, total boundary counts, n biological tags; never pool time endpoints as independent individuals.
effect.status_if_low: NOT_ESTIMABLE, no alternate threshold or source cohort.
effect.biological_interpretation: A positive dusk Protected→Rice source class routing excess is compatible with an diel agricultural/refuge habitat-use circuit, not proof feeding, roosting, hunting avoidance, competitive interaction, or active regulation. Arrival photoperiod is part of the ecological contrast; origin location and route still unobserved.

limitations: Second-stage test explicitly chosen after initial raw protected/rice directional counts, therefore exploratory and not independent confirmation.

Same public movement-endpoint source as already published Overton/Casazza day-night selection contrasts; compare novel cross-state transition predictions, do not claim original daytime use and habitat preference as new.
Reference availability is source-generated from actual geographical step origin; source lacks habitat at move origin, so p_t does not preserve state-specific spatial access.
Protected is a refuge-management category not uniquely interpreted as roost; rice is crop cover, not direct diet/feeding observation.
Day/night transitions may coincide with source sampling and movement-behaviour shifts; direction is not a randomized ecological cause.
